## Appearing in "His Hideous Heart"

**Featured Characters:**

*   [Hulk (Bruce Banner)](/wiki/Bruce_Banner_(Earth-616) "Bruce Banner (Earth-616)") (Possessed by the [One Below All](/wiki/One_Below_All_(Multiverse) "One Below All (Multiverse)")-possessed [Brian Banner](/wiki/Brian_Banner_(Earth-616) "Brian Banner (Earth-616)"))

## Synopsis for "His Hideous Heart"

Following his fatal battle with the Avengers that left him a charred corpse, Bruce Banner is captured by the U.S. Hulk Operations and sent to Shadow Base. The base's scientists dissect his body and place his organs and body parts in separate jars, including his head. They remove his heart during the daytime but once the [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun") goes down it, along with the rest of him, begins to change. With the use of an adamantium scalpel mounted on a 7 million dollar hydraulic arm, they manage to cut the heart in half. After a few minutes, both halves begin to beat.

The heart is presented to Dr. Clive, who asks his fellow scientists if they have any ideas on how and why it is still beating. He notices the Hulk's severed head trying to speak and taunts him with the fact he cannot talk without lungs. The Hulk simply responds by having his severed hand give Clive the finger. Clive picks up the heart to "play" with it. To his surprise, both halves pull themselves together. Clive and his assistant, Charlene McGowan, discuss the Hulk's powers of regeneration, specifically why his individual parts do not grow into new Hulks. Clive states they need to know what the rules are because, otherwise, how can they break them?

On board the Alpha Flight Space Station, Captain Marvel tells Jackie McGee that neither Alpha Flight or the Avengers know where the Hulk ended up after he was handed over to the government. Thaddeus Ross denies any knowledge, General Fortean, who requested that the Avengers bring the Hulk in, cannot be found, official requests are lost, and other contacts in Washington have been fired without reason. She wonders if the government lost the Hulk, or if they kidnapped him, but she believes that the negative press should put pressure on whoever has him. Additionally, she reinstates Walter Langkowski to active duty. Walter questions why Carol would want him back in the field since he can no longer turn into Sasquatch. Carol tells him that she does not need Sasquatch, she needs Walter Langkowski, a noted gamma expert with some insight into how the Hulk thinks. She wants Walter to head up a new task force to locate the Hulk: Gamma Flight.

Back at Shadow Base, Dr. Clive argues with General Fortean over the phone about Carol Danvers' public announcement of Gamma Flight and the sudden spotlight she has placed on the U.S. Hulk Operations. Fortean orders all Shadow Base staff to relocate to Site B. Clive tells Charlene to prep Del Frye for transport. He will deal with another one named "Red Dog" just as soon as he is finished with the Hulk.

Clive notices the Hulk's head is smiling at him. Clive starts taunting the Hulk by describing what they are going to do with him in graphic detail, but the head keeps smiling. He tells him that they are going to learn his secrets, how he can move, and what he can do. Clive stops mid-sentence because he suddenly realizes that the Hulk _allowed_ himself to be experimented on, since if they know what he is capable of, so would he. At that moment one of the Hulk's severed hands snaps its fingers. The resulting shockwave is powerful enough to shatter every glass jar in the lab. All of the Hulk's organs and body parts land on the floor and begin to pull themselves together around Clive. Clive begs for his life and tries to apologize for what he has done, but his cries fade out as he is absorbed into the Hulk's body. Now fully reformed, the Hulk grabs Clive's lab coat and tunnels his way out of the base. Charlene comes to Clive's lab to talk to him about Del Frye's tank mix, but only finds a massive hole in the floor.

The Hulk makes it to the surface and discovers that he is in northern New Mexico; ironically, close to "home". The [Sun](/wiki/Sun "Sun") had risen by the time the Hulk reached the surface, so he painfully transforms back into Banner. Donning Clive's lab coat, Bruce resumes his trek "home". He is overcome by an uneasy feeling like he has been infected. He feels certain that the Hulk crossed the line and took a life, and for a moment, he thinks he can hear his father's voice laughing at him from everywhere at once.

## Solicit Synopsis

• Bruce Banner is dead. His corpse has been dissected, his organs catalogued, and his inner workings are being studied by the scientists of Shadow Base.

• Bruce Banner is no longer a threat.

• That just leaves the IMMORTAL HULK...
